notes.meaning: Jesus had already ordered the evil spirit to leave the man. The demon had attacked him many times, giving him unnatural strength to snap chains and driving him out into lonely wastelands. Jesus showed deep mercy by stepping in to free someone in such awful misery.

Jesus asked the demon for its name, not because He did not know, but so the crowd could see how terrible the man's condition was. The demon answered "Legion," which was a Roman army unit of about six thousand soldiers. This meant thousands of evil spirits were tormenting this one man.

The demons begged Jesus not to banish them into the Abyss. The Abyss means the bottomless pit, the prison where fallen spirits are kept until final judgment. Even a whole army of demons knew they had to obey Jesus and feared His power.

A large herd of pigs was feeding nearby on the hillside. Because Jewish law considered pigs unclean, their presence showed this was a Gentile region. The demons begged to enter the animals, and Jesus permitted it, showing that evil spirits cannot do anything without God's permission.

The demons left the man and rushed into the herd of pigs. Immediately, the herd charged down the steep cliff into the lake and drowned. This shocking sight showed everyone the true goal of the demons, which was complete destruction.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern interpreters suggest the terrified man chased the pigs himself or that the herd panicked naturally, rather than actual evil spirits entering the animals.

notes.meaning: The men caring for the pigs saw what happened and ran away in shock. They hurried into the town and the surrounding farms to tell everyone the news. They feared what the pig owners would say about losing their property.

The local people went out to see the sight for themselves. When they reached Jesus, they found the formerly wild man sitting peacefully at Jesus' feet, wearing clothes and thinking clearly. Instead of rejoicing, the people were filled with fear at such mighty power.

Eyewitnesses explained the whole event to the newcomers. They described how the tormented man had been completely rescued and made well. God's saving power had turned a hopeless outcast into a healthy disciple.

The entire population of the area asked Jesus to leave because they were gripped by fear. They cared more about the financial loss of their pigs than the wonderful deliverance of their neighbor. Jesus did not force Himself on them, so He got into a boat to return across the lake.

The healed man pleaded to go with Jesus in the boat. He loved his rescuer and wanted to stay safely in His company. Yet Jesus gently denied his request because He had an important task for him to do at home.

Jesus told the man to return home and tell his family and neighbors how much God had done for him. The man obeyed and told the story throughout the whole town, proclaiming what Jesus had done. By speaking of Jesus' actions as God's work, the story showed that Jesus shares the divine power of God.

When Jesus sailed back across the lake to Galilee, a large crowd greeted Him with great joy. They had stayed along the shore waiting eagerly for His return. Unlike the people who drove Him away, these people were hungry to hear His teaching and receive His help.

A man named Jairus came through the crowd and bowed down at Jesus' feet. He was a synagogue leader, an important official who organized local Jewish worship. For a respected leader to kneel publicly showed his deep humility and urgent need.

Jairus was desperate because his only daughter was about twelve years old and dying. Jesus agreed to go with him, but the crowds pressed tightly around Him as He walked. The crush of people slowed His journey during this race against time.

In the crowd was a woman who had suffered from chronic bleeding for twelve long years. She had spent all her money on doctors, but none could cure her. Her sickness also made her ceremonially unclean, cutting her off from worship and community life.

The woman slipped up behind Jesus and touched the tassel on the edge of His outer robe. Pious Jewish men wore these tassels to remember God's commandments. The moment she touched it, her bleeding stopped, showing Christ's power to heal instantly without being made unclean Himself.

Jesus turned and asked who had touched Him, but everyone nearby denied it. Peter pointed out that the crowd was bumping and crushing against Him from every side. Jesus asked the question not out of ignorance, but to draw the healed woman out into the open.

Jesus insisted that someone had deliberately touched Him, because He felt healing power go out from Himself. Many people brushed against Him by accident, but only one reached out with trusting faith. Real faith connects directly with the living power of God.

Realizing she could not stay hidden, the woman came forward trembling and fell at Jesus' feet. Before the whole crowd, she explained why she had touched Him and how she was healed that very second. By speaking up, she received Jesus' open blessing and showed everyone God's goodness.

Jesus warmly called her "Daughter" and told her that her faith had saved and healed her. He gave her His blessing to go in peace, meaning complete wholeness of body and soul. He made sure she knew it was trust in Him, not a magical robe, that brought her health.

While Jesus was still speaking with the woman, a messenger came from Jairus's home. He reported that the little girl had just died, so there was no need to trouble the Teacher any further. To human eyes, all hope was completely gone.

Jesus heard the tragic news and spoke directly to the grieving father. He told Jairus not to be afraid, but simply to keep believing, and his daughter would be restored. Jesus encouraged him to trust God's power even in the face of death itself.

When Jesus arrived at the house, He kept the noisy crowd outside. He allowed only Peter, John, James, and the child's parents to enter the room where the body lay. These three disciples formed His closest circle and were chosen to witness His greatest miracles.

The house was filled with relatives and hired mourners weeping and wailing loudly. Jesus told them to stop crying because the girl was not dead, but only asleep. He called death "sleep" because her departure was only brief, and He was about to wake her up.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern writers suggest Jesus meant the words literally and that the girl had fallen into a deep coma or trance rather than dying.

notes.meaning: The mourners laughed in Jesus' face because they were certain the girl was dead. Their mocking laughter actually served a purpose for later readers. It proved beyond doubt that she had truly died, so her recovery was a genuine miracle.

Jesus sent the noisy mockers out of the room, leaving only the parents and His three disciples. Then He gently took the girl by the hand and spoke with commanding authority, telling the child to get up. His touch and voice carried the creative power of God.

Her spirit returned into her body, and she stood up immediately. Jesus then told her parents to give her something to eat. Giving her ordinary food proved that she was fully alive and completely healed from her illness.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early church writings preserved in Catholic tradition noted that her spirit returning showed her own personal soul was reunited with her physical body.

notes.meaning: The girl's parents were completely astonished by what had happened. Jesus strictly instructed them not to broadcast the details of the miracle. He wanted to protect the family's privacy and avoid wild crowds seeking spectacular signs instead of His message.
